stem:
Electrons in a vacuum are accelerated from rest through a potential difference (p.d.) *V* to form a beam. The electrons each have mass *m* and charge *q*.

The beam is incident on a graphite crystal that acts as a diffraction grating. After passing through the crystal, the beam reaches a fluorescent screen. An interference pattern is observed on this screen.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what this observation shows about the nature of electrons.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of *m*, *q* and *V*, for the momentum *p* of an electron in the beam.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The p.d. through which the electrons are accelerated is now increased to a greater value.

Describe and explain the effect of this change on the interference pattern observed.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead: The electrons are now accelerated through different values of *V*, resulting in pairs of corresponding values for *p* and the de Broglie wavelength λ.
parts.text:
On Fig. 9.1, sketch the variation of *p* with 1/λ.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the quantity represented by the gradient of the line in Fig. 9.1.

figures.caption: Fig. 9.1
figures.alt: Axes with arrows show *p* vertically and 1/λ horizontally, with zero marked at the origin and on both axes.
